taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): "a ... large, long-lived, native, perennial forb 1 to 2 feet (0.3-0.6 m) in height".

traits.life_span.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): "long-lived ... perennial forb".

traits.rosette.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): basal leaves "arise from a branched, underground caudex to form dense rosettes".

traits.leaf_shape.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): basal leaves "cordate to sagittate in outline", widest at their base, so deltate in the chart of plane shapes; "the cauline leaves are mostly lanceolate ... and much smaller than the basal leaves".

traits.leaf_margin.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): basal leaves "with entire margins".

traits.inflorescence.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): "Flowers are mostly solitary on long peduncles": one head to a stem.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): "Flowerheads are sunflower-like with strap-shaped ray flowers ... and tubular disc flowers".

traits.ray_length_m.note: FEIS's arrowleaf balsamroot review (McWilliams 2002, as Balsamorhiza sagittata, read 2026-10-15): ray flowers "1 to 2 inches (2.5-5 cm) long".

traits.ray_colour.note: Bright yellow rays, by eye; FEIS's "sunflower-like" heads (McWilliams 2002) give no colour in words.

generator.params.note: Oregon sunshine's program values, changed by hand for arrowleaf balsamroot: a dense rosette of large, long-stalked, arrowhead-shaped basal leaves from the caudex, and a few nearly leafless stems each ending in one big head (FEIS, McWilliams 2002). The head's size (flower_size 0.1 m) is the middle of the species-facts estimate of 6-12 cm across, which gives rays inside FEIS's 2.5-5 cm. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 45 cm at 4 years, the middle of FEIS's 0.3-0.6 m (McWilliams 2002). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey-green woolly leaves (FEIS: "wooly pubescence"); bright yellow sunflower-like heads.
